newsitem.title: MEXICO: WIND AND WUTHERING GREET OLYMPICS CHIEFS IN MEXICAN SUNSPOT.
newsitem.headline: WIND AND WUTHERING GREET OLYMPICS CHIEFS IN MEXICAN SUNSPOT.

text.p: Driving rain and howling wind have greeted the world's Olympic chiefs in this usually sweltering resort on Mexico's Caribbean coast, prompting apologies from Mexican officials and even a request for legislation to fix the weather.

After two days of downpour, Mario Villanueva Madrid, governor of the Mexican state of Quintana Roo where Cancun is located, said Thursday that Association of National Olympic Committees (ANOC) chief Mario Vasquez Rana had asked him to issue a decree banning rain.

"The burning sun that characterises Cancun and which had made itself scarce for us will doubtless be made up for by the hospitality with which we receive you," Education Minister Miguel Limon Rojas told ANOC and International Olympic Committee (IOC) members, by way of hopeful apology.

IOC director general Francois Carrard, referring to a brief break in the deluge, said he was glad he did not have to use a gondola to cross Cancun's flooded main drag on his way to brief reporters. The slate-grey heavens then opened again.
"The weather report is such that by Sunday late afternoon (the last day of the meetings) we may regard a majestic, colourful sunset over Mexico," Carrard said, "...As we are flying home."
